title: Gassner, From Brest-Litovsk via St. Germain to Sèvres

slides.title: What the article examines, and why it leaves out Versailles
slides.text: The aim: to illuminate the STARTING SITUATION OF THE RUSSIAN, HABSBURG AND OTTOMAN EMPIRES at the end of the First World War and to analyse the making of the PEACE TREATIES OF BREST-LITOVSK, ST GERMAIN AND SÈVRES, compare their provisions and place them in context. The German Empire and the Treaty of Versailles are DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT because they have already been the subject of numerous studies; the author concentrates on three treaties which all PLAYED A KEY ROLE IN THE DECLINE OF THE MULTI-ETHNIC EMPIRES. The framing sentence she quotes from the historian PATRICK COHRS: the First World War was ESSENTIALLY A WAR BETWEEN EMPIRES AND IMPERIAL STATES, INTO WHICH SMALLER STATES AND SUBJECT IMPERIAL POPULATIONS WERE DRAWN ON BOTH SIDES.

cards.q: Which three peace treaties does Gassner compare, and why does she leave out Versailles?
cards.a: Brest-Litovsk, St Germain-en-Laye and Sèvres — all three played a key role in the decline of the MULTI-ETHNIC EMPIRES (Russian, Habsburg, Ottoman). She deliberately leaves out Versailles and the German Empire because they have already been the subject of numerous studies.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Russia: from the Decree on Peace to Brest
slides.text: Russia had already lost important western territories in 1915 — CONGRESS POLAND, COURLAND AND LITHUANIA — in the GREAT RETREAT that followed the Austro-German breakthrough at GORLICE AND TARNÓW. In 1917, after three years of war without success, support for Nicholas II collapsed and he was forced to abdicate by the FEBRUARY REVOLUTION. The OCTOBER REVOLUTION (6–8 November, or 24–26 October by the Russian calendar) brought the Bolsheviks to power. ECONOMICALLY RUSSIA NO LONGER EXISTED, and the Bolsheviks needed time and all their resources to stabilise their own rule. ON 8 NOVEMBER, the day after the successful coup, the new government issued the 'DECREE ON PEACE', which ABOLISHED SECRET DIPLOMACY, PROPOSED AN IMMEDIATE GENERAL PEACE WITHOUT ANNEXATIONS OR INDEMNITIES AND DEMANDED THAT EVERY NATION BE GRANTED THE RIGHT OF SELF-DETERMINATION. On 28 November Lenin and Trotsky issued an official peace offer; the Central Powers agreed on 29 November. And now what matters for the Habsburg side: THE RUSSIAN PEACE PROPOSAL RESTED ON NATIONAL SELF-DETERMINATION AND THEREFORE POSED A RISK TO THE MULTI-ETHNIC HABSBURG MONARCHY — but the monarchy was under domestic pressure, the population was weary of the war, and the growing Social Democrats openly sympathised with Lenin's proposal, which is one reason why the foreign minister COUNT CZERNIN agreed to negotiations at once. An armistice was concluded ON 15 DECEMBER 1917; by then UKRAINE, THE FINNS AND THE KAZAKHS had already declared independence and the CRIMEAN PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC, THE FIRST SECULAR MUSLIM STATE TO DECLARE SOVEREIGNTY, had come into being. Negotiations began at Brest-Litovsk on 22 December.

cards.q: What did the Bolshevik 'Decree on Peace' of 8 November 1917 contain?
cards.a: The abolition of SECRET DIPLOMACY, a proposal of an IMMEDIATE GENERAL PEACE WITHOUT ANNEXATIONS OR INDEMNITIES, and the demand that EVERY NATION BE GRANTED THE RIGHT OF SELF-DETERMINATION.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: Why was the Russian peace proposal dangerous for Austria-Hungary, and why did it enter negotiations anyway?
cards.a: Because it rested on NATIONAL SELF-DETERMINATION, which threatened the multi-ethnic monarchy. It entered them because it was under domestic pressure: the population was weary of war and the growing Social Democrats openly sympathised with Lenin's proposal — which is why Count Czernin agreed to negotiate at once.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Austria-Hungary: disintegration before the armistice
slides.text: Austria-Hungary suffered not only bitter defeats but was also weakened by UNRESOLVED NATIONAL CONFLICTS. By the end of October 1918 the army was in such a state that the command had to sue for an armistice; the monarchy signed it ON 3 NOVEMBER 1918 AT VILLA GIUSTI NEAR PADUA. And here is the crucial chronology: BY THE TIME THE ARMISTICE WAS CONCLUDED, THE MONARCHY HAD ALREADY DISINTEGRATED. Inspired by Wilson's Fourteen Points, the CZECHOSLOVAK REPUBLIC was proclaimed on 28 OCTOBER 1918 and the STATE OF SLOVENES, CROATS AND SERBS the following day; on 31 OCTOBER HUNGARY renounced the real union, whereby the monarchy fell apart. The German-speaking members of the Imperial Council formed a PROVISIONAL NATIONAL ASSEMBLY on 21 October and resolved to found the REPUBLIC OF GERMAN-AUSTRIA, proclaimed on 30 OCTOBER 1918. The name GERMAN-AUSTRIA (DEUTSCHÖSTERREICH) was meant both to signal a certain distance from the monarchy and to affirm adherence to the German nation. And the legal dispute that follows from it: in post-war Austria the prevailing view — shared by HANS KELSEN in an opinion of 29 November 1918 — was that GERMAN-AUSTRIA IS A NEWLY FOUNDED STATE AND THEREFORE CANNOT BE REGARDED AS THE LEGAL SUCCESSOR OF THE HABSBURG MONARCHY. THIS 'DISCONTINUITY THESIS' MET WITH ACCEPTANCE ONLY IN GREAT BRITAIN and the other Allied powers rejected it — led by FRANCE, which regarded Austria together with Hungary as the CLEAR LEGAL SUCCESSOR of the monarchy.

terms.def: The Austrian view (Kelsen's included) that German-Austria is a newly founded state and therefore not the legal successor of the monarchy. Only Britain accepted it; France and the others rejected it.

cards.q: What is the 'discontinuity thesis' and how did it fare?
cards.a: The view prevailing in post-war Austria — held by Hans Kelsen in his opinion of 29 November 1918 — that GERMAN-AUSTRIA IS A NEWLY FOUNDED STATE and therefore not the legal successor of the Habsburg monarchy. It found acceptance ONLY IN GREAT BRITAIN; the other Allies rejected it, led by France, which regarded Austria and Hungary as clear legal successors.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: In what order did the Habsburg monarchy disintegrate in the autumn of 1918?
cards.a: 21 October, the provisional national assembly of German-speaking deputies; 28 October, the Czechoslovak Republic proclaimed; 29 October, the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs; 30 October, the Republic of German-Austria proclaimed; 31 October, Hungary renounced the real union. Only on 3 November was the armistice signed — BY WHICH TIME THE MONARCHY HAD ALREADY DISINTEGRATED.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: The Ottoman Empire and the Armistice of Mudros
slides.text: That Turkey would enter the war on the side of the Central Powers was not clear from the outset: only when negotiations about possible TURKISH NEUTRALITY foundered on Turkish counter-demands — THE ABOLITION OF THE CAPITULATIONS and THE DELIVERY OF THE ALREADY PAID-FOR WARSHIPS ORDERED IN BRITAIN — did the Ottoman Empire enter the war on 24 OCTOBER 1914. (The CAPITULATIONS were special treaties between the Ottoman Empire and most Christian states of Europe from the early modern period, which created a SYSTEM OF EXTRATERRITORIAL PRIVILEGES in favour of many European states.) In the fourth year of the war the British advanced into much of Mesopotamia and Palestine and in 1917 took Baghdad and Jerusalem; the Ottoman army shrank TO A FIFTH OF ITS ORIGINAL STRENGTH and on 30 OCTOBER 1918 there was nothing for it but to sign an armistice IN MUDROS BAY ON LEMNOS. The peace negotiations were conducted BILATERALLY BETWEEN THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE AND GREAT BRITAIN; the other Allies were not present. By the Armistice of Mudros the empire was in effect REDUCED TO ASIA MINOR, since the Hejaz, Yemen, Syria and Mesopotamia — and also Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and Egypt, which by then belonged to the empire only formally — were definitively lost. AND THE DIFFERENCE THAT DECIDED EVERYTHING ELSE: UNLIKE IN THE NEGOTIATIONS WITH AUSTRIA-HUNGARY, NO REFERENCE WAS MADE TO WILSON'S FOURTEEN POINTS IN THE CASE OF TURKEY — THE ALLIES WERE THEREFORE BOUND BY NOTHING.

terms.def: Treaties between the Ottoman Empire and European states from the early modern period, establishing a system of extraterritorial privileges for foreigners in the empire.

cards.q: Why did the Ottoman Empire enter the war, and what did the neutrality negotiations founder on?
cards.a: On Turkish counter-demands: the ABOLITION OF THE CAPITULATIONS (the system of extraterritorial privileges of the European states) and THE DELIVERY OF THE ALREADY PAID-FOR WARSHIPS ordered in Britain. Only when those negotiations failed did the empire enter the war on 24 October 1914 alongside Germany and Austria-Hungary.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: How did the Ottoman armistice differ from the Austrian one, and why did that matter?
cards.a: At Mudros NO REFERENCE WAS MADE TO WILSON'S FOURTEEN POINTS AT ALL, so THE ALLIES WERE BOUND BY NOTHING — whereas the Austrian armistice rested on them. Moreover it was negotiated BILATERALLY with Great Britain alone, without the other Allies.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Interests at Brest and interests regarding Austria
slides.text: A methodological caveat the author puts up front: ALL THREE TREATIES AND THE INTERESTS BEHIND THEM CAN BE COMPARED ONLY TO A VERY LIMITED EXTENT, BECAUSE BREST-LITOVSK WAS MORE OR LESS DICTATED BY THE CENTRAL POWERS, WHEREAS THE PARIS TREATIES WERE DICTATED BY THE ALLIES. AT BREST the main common interest of Austria and Germany was TO DETACH CONGRESS POLAND, COURLAND AND LITHUANIA FROM RUSSIA PERMANENTLY; at first they agreed NOT TO SUPPORT UKRAINIAN ASPIRATIONS TO INDEPENDENCE, but at the end of December Czernin began to change his mind. FOR AUSTRIA IN PARIS the question was chiefly HOW FAR REPARATIONS COULD BE DEMANDED OF AUSTRIA. The British and the Americans appeared accommodating and, apart from reparations, had no economic interests. EVEN THE FRENCH INTEREST WAS IN FACT LIMITED: France directed all its energy to defeating its arch-rival Germany and was interested in Austria only so far AS THAT SERVED TO WEAKEN GERMANY. This showed itself particularly in the question of union with Germany: THE 'ANSCHLUSS' WAS NOT A PRODUCT OF THE FIRST WORLD WAR, but the collapse of the monarchy gave it new urgency, especially since German-Austria was not regarded as ECONOMICALLY VIABLE. In the Treaty of St Germain France pushed through the PROHIBITION OF UNION — and in that connection the state's name had to be changed from German-Austria to Austria. Important for France was SUPPORT FOR CZECHOSLOVAKIA, which both formed a good BUFFER AGAINST APPROACHING BOLSHEVISM and, through its territorial claims, WEAKENED GERMANY — which is why France supported all its territorial demands against Austria as well. Of the principal Allies, only ITALY had a genuine interest of its own in Austria, namely territorial claims, which in the absence of competing interests it successfully pushed through.

cards.q: Why can Brest-Litovsk and the Paris treaties not be fully compared?
cards.a: Because BREST-LITOVSK WAS MORE OR LESS DICTATED BY THE CENTRAL POWERS, WHEREAS THE PARIS TREATIES WERE DICTATED BY THE ALLIES — they are treaties signed by opposite victors, and therefore differ in their drafting history, structure, rhetoric and style.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What interest did France have in Austria?
cards.a: A limited and derivative one: it directed its energy to defeating Germany and was interested in Austria ONLY SO FAR AS THAT SERVED TO WEAKEN GERMANY. Hence it pushed through the PROHIBITION OF THE ANSCHLUSS (and with it the change of the state's name from German-Austria to Austria) and supported all the territorial demands of Czechoslovakia, which was both a buffer against Bolshevism and a weakening of Germany.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Interests in the Ottoman Empire: why it took two years
slides.text: While the interests of the great powers in Austria were limited, THE INTERESTS IN THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE WERE TOO DIVERSE TO BE MANAGED — which is why signing the Turkish treaty took ALMOST TWO YEARS, whereas with Russia and Austria it was done within a few months of the armistice. BRITAIN: it had on the Indian subcontinent a colonial empire comprising today's India, Pakistan and Bangladesh — and therefore SEVERAL MILLION MUSLIMS whose interests it had to take into account; in the dispute between the SHARIF OF MECCA and the SULTAN the 'Indian Muslims' sided with the sultan, which did not make Britain's position easier when it had itself allied with the anti-Ottoman sharif. It wanted free, secure and permanent access to India, for which an INDEPENDENT ARMENIA was to serve as a buffer against Russia. Since the war the powers had become ever more aware of the IMPORTANCE OF OIL, which led Britain to demand CONTROL OVER THE EUPHRATES AND TIGRIS and an extension of influence in Baghdad and Basra — a continuous belt of territory FROM THE MEDITERRANEAN TO THE INDUS was to be under British control. Since opening a consulate in Palestine in 1838, Britain had acted as the PROTECTING POWER OF THE JEWS (AND PROTESTANTS) in the Holy Land, as a counterweight to France, which traditionally saw itself as the protector of Catholics in the Middle East. From LLOYD GEORGE's accession in December 1916 exclusive British control of Palestine became one of the main aims, because Palestine was to provide a SECURE LAND CONNECTION BETWEEN BRITISH EGYPT AND A FUTURE BRITISH MESOPOTAMIA. For this it was first necessary to REMOVE THE SYKES-PICOT AGREEMENT and stop France in Palestine — for which the Jews living in Palestine and the BALFOUR DECLARATION were to serve. And finally the personal factor: Lloyd George had great personal sympathy for the Greek prime minister VENIZELOS, which coincided with public opinion — since the ARMENIAN GENOCIDE an intensely ANTI-TURKISH (and pro-Armenian) MOOD had spread among the British public.

terms.def: The secret delimitation of British and French colonial spheres of influence in the Middle East in the event of an Ottoman defeat; Russia and Italy later joined.

cards.q: Why did concluding the treaty with Turkey take almost two years, while with Russia and Austria it took months?
cards.a: Because THE ALLIES' INTERESTS IN THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE WERE TOO DIVERSE TO BE MANAGED — British and French interests clashed openly from Mudros onwards, and to these were added the claims of Italy, Greece, Armenia and the Kurds.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: List the British interests in the Ottoman Empire.
cards.a: Secure access to India (with Armenia as a buffer against Russia); regard for the several million Muslims within its own empire; OIL, that is control over the Euphrates and Tigris and influence in Baghdad and Basra; a continuous belt from the Mediterranean to the Indus; exclusive control of Palestine as the land bridge between Egypt and a future Mesopotamia — for which the Sykes-Picot Agreement had to be removed and the Balfour Declaration used.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: Why did France want to preserve the Ottoman Empire?
cards.a: For economic reasons: ABOUT 60 PER CENT OF THE PRE-WAR OTTOMAN PUBLIC DEBT (Dette publique ottomane) WAS HELD BY FRENCH PRIVATE CREDITORS. As the Catholic protecting power of Christians in the Middle East it also claimed territories with Christian minorities — Syria and Lebanon. But since the priority was to weaken Germany, it had to give way to British demands on the Turkish question and concentrated on preventing British control of the Straits.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Brest-Litovsk: a collision of two worlds
slides.text: Unlike the other treaties, the armistice and the peace negotiations took place AT THE SAME PLACE and flowed into one another. As BORISLAV CHERNEV aptly described it, from December 1917 to March 1918 TWO IMMENSELY DIFFERENT WORLDS MET AT THE TABLE: REVOLUTIONARY TACTICS CROSSED SWORDS WITH IMPERIAL CABINET DIPLOMACY FOR THE FIRST TIME. On one side representatives of the European high aristocracy, on the other Russian revolutionaries, some of them ordinary workers rewarded with important posts for their part in the revolution. And the atmosphere was QUITE UNLIKE THAT BETWEEN VICTORS AND VANQUISHED IN PARIS: ESPECIALLY IN THE FIRST ROUND RUSSIA WAS FORMALLY TREATED AS AN EQUAL PARTNER and joint dinners were held. The German state secretary RICHARD VON KÜHLMANN recorded of the first of these an anecdote that illustrates the collision: the Russians had made a peace delegate of a woman straight from Siberia, MADAME BIZENKO, who had shot a governor-general disliked by the left and, under tsarist practice, had not been executed but sentenced to life. 'THIS LADY, WHO LOOKED LIKE AN ELDERLY HOUSEKEEPER, EVIDENTLY A QUITE UNREFLECTING FANATIC, TOLD PRINCE LEOPOLD OF BAVARIA OVER DINNER HOW SHE HAD CARRIED OUT THE ASSASSINATION. HOLDING THE MENU IN HER LEFT HAND, SHE DEMONSTRATED HOW SHE HAD HANDED THE GOVERNOR — „HE WAS A WICKED MAN“, SHE ADDED BY WAY OF EXPLANATION — AN EXTENSIVE MEMORANDUM AND AT THE SAME TIME SHOT HIM IN THE STOMACH WITH THE REVOLVER HELD IN HER RIGHT. PRINCE LEOPOLD, WITH HIS USUAL FRIENDLY COURTESY, LISTENED WITH RAPT ATTENTION, AS THOUGH THE MURDERESS'S REPORT INTERESTED HIM MOST KEENLY.'

cards.q: How did the atmosphere at Brest-Litovsk differ from that in Paris?
cards.a: At Brest, especially in the first round, RUSSIA WAS FORMALLY TREATED AS AN EQUAL PARTNER and joint dinners were held — 'revolutionary tactics crossed swords with imperial cabinet diplomacy for the first time'. In Paris, by contrast, the Austrian delegation was housed in a separate quarter which it could leave only accompanied by an officer, and was treated more like prisoners than diplomats.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Brest: the Ukrainian card and 'no war, no peace'
slides.text: The Russian delegation issued a DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES — peace without annexations, the right of self-determination, no reparations — and since the Central Powers had no joint proposal, that declaration became the basis of the first round. On 25 December the powers issued counter-proposals; Austria-Hungary wanted to sign at once and threatened a SEPARATE PEACE, but GERMANY WAS INDIFFERENT, since Austria was dependent on its ally in any case. The second round was marked by THE RUSSIAN ATTEMPT TO DRAG OUT THE NEGOTIATIONS IN THE HOPE THAT THE REVOLUTION WOULD MEANWHILE SPREAD TO WESTERN EUROPE. Besides the general fear of revolution and military considerations, it was FEAR OF A SHORTAGE OF GRAIN DELIVERIES that led the Central Powers — especially Austria-Hungary — to sign a SEPARATE PEACE TREATY WITH THE UKRAINIAN PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC ON 9 FEBRUARY 1918, recognising its sovereignty. (Soviet Russia regarded the Ukrainian People's Republic as a 'bourgeois republic' and a 'creature of the Central Powers' and sent troops there — so by the time the delegations met at Brest, WAR WAS ALREADY UNDER WAY BETWEEN UKRAINE AND SOVIET RUSSIA.) After the peace with Ukraine, Russia broke off the negotiations: TROTSKY threatened to order full demobilisation on all fronts BUT NOT TO SIGN A PEACE — the formula that became known as 'NO WAR, NO PEACE'. Germany therefore treated the armistice as lapsed and on 17 February launched Operation 'FAUSTSCHLAG'; the Russian forces offered no serious resistance and the powers soon took territory in Estonia, Latvia, Belarus and Ukraine. ON 3 MARCH 1918 RUSSIA SIGNED THE TREATY UNDER PROTEST — in its view it was an ANNEXATIONIST AND IMPERIALIST PEACE WHICH, UNDER THE PRETEXT OF LIBERATING THE BORDERLANDS OF RUSSIA, TURNED THEM INTO GERMAN PROVINCES AND UNDERMINED THEIR RIGHT OF SELF-DETERMINATION.

terms.def: Trotsky's formula: demobilise on all fronts but do not sign a peace. Germany answered it by resuming the war (Operation Faustschlag).

cards.q: What did Trotsky's 'no war, no peace' mean and how did it end?
cards.a: He threatened to order full demobilisation on all fronts BUT NOT TO SIGN A PEACE. Germany therefore treated the armistice as lapsed and on 17 February 1918 launched Operation FAUSTSCHLAG; the Russian forces offered no serious resistance and the Central Powers took Estonia, Latvia, Belarus and Ukraine. On 3 March Russia signed the treaty UNDER PROTEST.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: Why did the Central Powers conclude a separate peace with Ukraine?
cards.a: Besides the fear of revolution and military considerations, chiefly out of FEAR OF A SHORTAGE OF GRAIN DELIVERIES, especially in Austria-Hungary. By the treaty of 9 February 1918 they recognised the sovereignty of the Ukrainian People's Republic — even though war was already under way between it and Soviet Russia.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: The Paris conference: who was admitted and who was not
slides.text: The PRELIMINARY PEACE CONFERENCE opened on 18 JANUARY 1919. All states that had been at war with the German Empire, or had at least broken off relations with it, were admitted — THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE AND AUSTRIA-HUNGARY WERE NOT ADMITTED. And as to Russia: THE PRINCIPAL ALLIED AND ASSOCIATED POWERS PRETENDED IT DID NOT EXIST. For all matters concerning the former monarchy and the Ottoman Empire, the SUPREME COUNCIL, known as the 'COUNCIL OF TEN', composed of the heads of government and foreign ministers of the principal powers, was initially competent. THE FIRST HALF OF 1919 WAS DOMINATED BY DRAFTING THE TREATY WITH GERMANY; only afterwards did the powers turn to Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire.

cards.q: Who was and was not admitted to the Paris conference?
cards.a: All states that had been at war with the German Empire or had at least broken off relations with it were admitted. THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE AND AUSTRIA-HUNGARY WERE NOT ADMITTED — and as to Russia, the principal powers PRETENDED IT DID NOT EXIST.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Austria in Paris and what it negotiated
slides.text: The Austrian delegation led by the Social Democratic State Chancellor KARL RENNER expected an invitation at the beginning of 1919, but was summoned ONLY IN MAY, when the treaty with Germany was already taking final shape. On 12 May the seven-member delegation left for Paris, where it was housed in a SEPARATE QUARTER WHICH IT COULD LEAVE ONLY ACCOMPANIED BY AN OFFICER — unlike the Russian delegation at Brest, it was treated MORE LIKE PRISONERS THAN DIPLOMATIC REPRESENTATIVES. On 2 June it received a first, still incomplete draft (the financial, military and reparation provisions were missing and the political ones were incomplete especially as regards Italy) and a fortnight to comment, which it did by memoranda with counter-proposals; to strengthen its negotiating position, the STATE SECRETARY FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS OTTO BAUER, a strong supporter of the Anschluss, EVEN RESIGNED. On 6 August the Allies' detailed reply arrived, from which it was clear that PARTIAL IMPROVEMENTS HAD BEEN ACHIEVED: Austria remained responsible for the war (art. 177), but THE FINANCIAL PROVISIONS NOW TOOK ACCOUNT OF THE DISSOLUTION OF THE MONARCHY, and the CONFISCATION OF THE PROPERTY of German-Austrian citizens in the territory of the monarchy was dropped. On the question of nationality the decisive criterion was — unlike in the other treaties — not habitual residence but HEIMATRECHT, the right of domicile (a person's belonging to a particular municipality, determined by descent and inherited, introduced in Austria in 1849 and abolished only in 1939). Territorially, Austria was essentially reduced to the territory from which it had emerged in the Middle Ages, and from August it was clear that SOUTH TYROL WOULD GO TO ITALY. But — and this is the point — AUSTRIA SURPRISINGLY GAINED NEW TERRITORY: the German-speaking WESTERN HUNGARIAN TERRITORY, today's BURGENLAND, unforeseen in the first draft. It can be read as generosity on the part of the Allies, who hoped that Austria would help suppress communism in Hungary. THE RESULT: AUSTRIA WAS THE ONLY DEFEATED STATE OF THE FIRST WORLD WAR TO MAKE A TERRITORIAL GAIN. On 10 SEPTEMBER 1919 Renner signed the Treaty of St Germain-en-Laye.

terms.def: The right of domicile: a person's belonging to a particular municipality, determined by descent and inherited, distinct from actual residence. At St Germain it governed nationality instead of habitual residence.

cards.q: By what criterion was nationality determined in the Treaty of St Germain, and how did that differ from the other treaties?
cards.a: By HEIMATRECHT, the right of domicile — a person's belonging to a particular municipality, determined by descent and inherited, distinct from actual residence (introduced 1849, abolished 1939). The other peace treaties proceeded from HABITUAL RESIDENCE.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: How is it possible that Austria gained territory?
cards.a: It received the German-speaking Western Hungarian territory, today's BURGENLAND, which was not in the first draft — apparently as generosity on the part of the Allies, who hoped Austria would help suppress communism in Hungary. AUSTRIA WAS THE ONLY DEFEATED STATE OF THE FIRST WORLD WAR TO MAKE A TERRITORIAL GAIN.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What did the Austrian delegation achieve by commenting on the draft?
cards.a: Partial improvements: the financial provisions began to TAKE ACCOUNT OF THE DISSOLUTION OF THE MONARCHY and the CONFISCATION OF THE PROPERTY of German-Austrian citizens in the monarchy's territory was dropped. Responsibility for the war (art. 177) nevertheless remained. To strengthen the position, Otto Bauer, a strong supporter of the Anschluss, even resigned.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: The Ottomans in Paris: a confident delegation and a postponement
slides.text: On 17 JUNE 1919, a few weeks after the occupation of SMYRNA by Greek troops, a four-member Ottoman delegation headed by the sultan's brother-in-law and Grand Vizier DAMAD FERID PASHA arrived in Paris and was allowed to appear before the 'Council of Ten' the same day. It appeared CONFIDENT: its main concern was to avert the 'DISMEMBERMENT' of the empire, and it showed willingness to negotiate only on the question of Egypt and Cyprus. It argued that THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE HAD FOR CENTURIES BEEN A GUARANTEE OF SECURITY AND PROSPERITY ON THE EUROPEAN, AFRICAN AND ASIAN CONTINENTS, and that the borders of the Muslim empire should correspond to THE BORDERS OF 1878, with the region of MOSUL and parts of Iranian and Russian territory to be returned to the sultanate. BRITAIN AND FRANCE WERE TAKEN ABACK BY THESE UNCOMPROMISING, ALMOST ARROGANT DEMANDS. A few days later the conference decided TO POSTPONE THE NEGOTIATIONS until the USA decided whether it would take over part of Turkey as a mandate — and the negotiations therefore stood still FROM JULY TO NOVEMBER 1919. (Only the Thracian question could not be postponed, being necessary to fix the borders in southern Bulgaria.) That postponement decided everything: MEANWHILE THE SITUATION IN TURKEY CHANGED FUNDAMENTALLY.

cards.q: What did the Ottoman delegation bring to Paris and how did it turn out?
cards.a: Confidently it sought to avert the 'dismemberment' of the empire, arguing that the empire had for centuries guaranteed security on three continents; it demanded the borders of 1878 and the return of Mosul. The British and the French were taken aback by that almost arrogant intransigence and POSTPONED the negotiations from July to November 1919 pending an American decision on a mandate — and that postponement gave Kemal his opening.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Mustafa Kemal: a second government beside the one negotiating
slides.text: In the regions threatened with an Armenian or Greek takeover, especially in CILICIA, local resistance groups formed, and in that new movement MUSTAFA KEMAL, the later Atatürk, already known for the successful defence of the GALLIPOLI PENINSULA in 1915, rose rapidly. When he was sent to Anatolia in May 1919 TO DISARM THE REMAINING UNITS UNDER THE ARMISTICE, HE DEFIED THE SULTAN'S ORDER AND LEFT THE ARMY — and considerable numbers of the soldiers in Anatolia left with him. In the summer of 1919 the CONGRESS OF ERZURUM was held, at which Kemal described the government in Istanbul as a 'HOSTAGE OF THE OCCUPYING POWERS'. The Allies IGNORED domestic developments in Turkey — including the fact that on 23 APRIL 1920 Kemal convened a NATIONAL ASSEMBLY IN ANKARA which made him its president, that he DECLARED THE SULTANATE ABOLISHED and appointed a government opposed both to the sultan and to the Allies. Hence Gassner's conclusion: ON 10 AUGUST 1920, IN ONE OF THE EXHIBITION HALLS OF THE FAMOUS PORCELAIN WORKS AT SÈVRES, A PEACE TREATY WAS SIGNED WITH A CONTRACTING PARTY THAT IN REALITY NO LONGER EXISTED. The historian PHILIP MARSHALL BROWN wrote of it: 'THE TREATY OF SÈVRES WAS AS FRAGILE AS THE PORCELAIN OF THAT NAME, ALAS WITHOUT ITS CHARM.'

cards.q: How did a second government arise in Turkey beside the one negotiating in Paris?
cards.a: Mustafa Kemal was sent to Anatolia in May 1919 to disarm units under the armistice, but HE DEFIED THE SULTAN'S ORDER AND LEFT THE ARMY, together with a large part of the soldiers. At the Congress of Erzurum he called the Istanbul government a 'hostage of the occupying powers'; on 23 April 1920 he convened a National Assembly in Ankara, declared the sultanate abolished and appointed his own government.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: How does Gassner sum up the signing of the Treaty of Sèvres, and what did Brown write about it?
cards.a: That on 10 August 1920, in an exhibition hall of the porcelain works at Sèvres, A PEACE TREATY WAS SIGNED WITH A CONTRACTING PARTY THAT IN REALITY NO LONGER EXISTED. Brown: 'The Treaty of Sèvres was as fragile as the porcelain of that name, alas without its charm.'
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: London and San Remo: how the Middle East was divided
slides.text: At the LONDON CONFERENCE (12 February – 10 April 1920) the project of a neutralised 'FREE STATE OF THE STRAITS' on the Danzig model fell through; the milder variant of DEMILITARISED STRAITS UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF AN INTERNATIONAL COMMISSION prevailed. The French demand for financial control over Turkey was met in exchange for the British proposal of a FORMAL RENUNCIATION OF REPARATION CLAIMS; an INTER-ALLIED FINANCIAL COMMISSION was set up. Reports from Cilicia, where the Kemalists were gaining ground, hastened a decision: ON 5 MARCH 1920 THE ALLIES RESOLVED TO OCCUPY CONSTANTINOPLE — the city was formally to be left to Turkey for the time being, but was to serve as a kind of 'HOSTAGE' FOR GOOD BEHAVIOUR: should there be further uprisings or massacres, the powers would reconsider their decision. On Smyrna the powers increasingly distanced themselves from Greece, but the Kemalist gains raised serious doubt whether a harsh treaty could be enforced in Turkey at all: THE REPORT OF MARSHAL FOCH FOR THE INTER-ALLIED COMMAND STATED THAT THE TREATY WOULD NOT BE ENFORCEABLE UNLESS SOME 325,000 MEN WERE PUT INTO THE FIELD — which neither Britain nor France was willing to do. Here Greece again offered itself as a 'SAVIOUR', claiming it would defeat the Turkish nationalists alone if need be, and in June 1920 it was charged with occupying EASTERN THRACE; VENIZELOS'S MEGALI IDEA thus seemed for a moment fulfilled. Turkey was to renounce all rights to LIBYA, TUNISIA, MOROCCO AND SUDAN; EGYPT was to become a British protectorate. On SYRIA it was agreed that FRANCE WOULD RECEIVE THE MANDATE FOR SYRIA AND BRITAIN FOR PALESTINE AND MESOPOTAMIA, with the Mosul oil more or less shared. AND ON THE KURDS THERE WAS A REVERSAL: LLOYD GEORGE NO LONGER DEFENDED AN INDEPENDENT KURDISH STATE. At the conference in SAN REMO (from 18 April 1920) Britain and France then jointly decided to CREATE A KURDISH AUTONOMOUS REGION — THE KURDISH DREAM OF A STATE OF THEIR OWN WAS NOT REALISED — and they DISAPPOINTED ARMENIA TOO, leaving the young Armenian state more or less to itself. Behind the scenes the SAN REMO OIL AGREEMENT was concluded between France and Britain WITHOUT AMERICAN PARTICIPATION: FRANCE WOULD GIVE UP MOSUL, WHICH TOGETHER WITH THE VILAYETS OF BAGHDAD AND BASRA WOULD PROVISIONALLY BE INCORPORATED INTO THE BRITISH MANDATE TERRITORY OF MESOPOTAMIA, and in return France would SHARE IN THE EXTRACTION OF MOSUL OIL.

terms.def: The Greek programme of territorial expansion at the expense of the Ottoman Empire, pursued by Venizelos at the Paris conference.

cards.q: Why was the Treaty of Sèvres unenforceable from the start? Give the figure.
cards.a: Because according to the report of MARSHAL FOCH for the inter-Allied command, enforcing it would have required putting some 325,000 MEN into the field — which neither Britain nor France was willing to do. Hence the acceptance of Greece's offer to defeat the Turkish nationalists itself.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: How did the Kurds and the Armenians fare?
cards.a: Both badly. At San Remo Britain and France agreed to create only a KURDISH AUTONOMOUS REGION — the Kurdish dream of a state of their own was not realised, after Lloyd George in London withdrew his support for a Kurdish state. And Armenia the powers left MORE OR LESS TO ITSELF, although both had previously supported an independent Armenia.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What did the San Remo oil agreement contain?
cards.a: It was concluded between France and Britain WITHOUT AMERICAN PARTICIPATION: France would give up MOSUL, which together with the vilayets of Baghdad and Basra would provisionally be incorporated into the British mandate territory of Mesopotamia, and in return France would SHARE IN THE EXTRACTION OF MOSUL OIL.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: Why and how was Constantinople occupied?
cards.a: On 5 March 1920, because of Kemalist gains in Cilicia. The city was formally to be left to Turkey for the time being, but was to serve as a 'HOSTAGE' FOR GOOD BEHAVIOUR: should there be further uprisings or massacres, the powers would reconsider. It is the symbol of the fact that the Allies aimed at the defeat of the empire — Constantinople was occupied, unlike Vienna or Berlin.

slides.title: Brest-Litovsk as a text
slides.text: Signed MORE THAN A YEAR BEFORE THE PARIS TREATIES, at a time when the war was still raging in full. The signatories: SOVIET RUSSIA on one side and the GERMAN EMPIRE, AUSTRIA-HUNGARY, BULGARIA AND THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE on the other. It has ONLY FOURTEEN ARTICLES, and is thus far shorter than the Paris treaties, although Russia had to sign a SUPPLEMENTARY AGREEMENT of about 35 articles with each power (restoration of diplomatic and consular relations, restoration of political treaties, restoration of private-law relations, compensation for civilian losses, exchange of prisoners, care for repatriates, amnesty). The difference is visible in the very first article: BREST HAS NO PREAMBLE, and art. 1 provides NEUTRALLY that Germany, Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria and Turkey on one side and Russia on the other declare THAT THE STATE OF WAR BETWEEN THEM HAS ENDED and that they have resolved to live henceforth in peace — WHEREAS THE PARIS TREATIES EXPLAIN IN THE VERY FIRST PARAGRAPH OF THE PREAMBLE THAT THE STATE OF WAR AROSE FROM HOSTILITIES BEGUN BY THE CENTRAL POWER IN QUESTION. Brest CONTAINS NO PROVISIONS ON WAR INDEMNITIES OR REPARATIONS — the most interesting provisions are therefore the territorial cessions. ARTICLE 3 detached from Russian sovereignty POLAND, LITHUANIA, COURLAND AND PART OF LIVONIA and granted them a LIMITED RIGHT OF SELF-DETERMINATION UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF AUSTRIA-HUNGARY AND GERMANY. In the Caucasus the territory Russia had taken from the Ottoman Empire in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78 — ARDAHAN, KARS AND BATUMI — was to be returned; Russia undertook to do everything to evacuate eastern Anatolia (art. 4). ART. 5 ordered the DEMOBILISATION of the Russian army and fleet, ART. 6 obliged Russia TO CONCLUDE PEACE WITH THE UKRAINIAN PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC IMMEDIATELY and to evacuate Estonia, Livonia, Finland and the Åland Islands (Estonia and Livonia were then occupied by German police units and effectively placed under German administration). ART. 7 declared PERSIA AND AFGHANISTAN free and independent countries; ART. 9 contained a MUTUAL RENUNCIATION OF COMPENSATION for the war. IN ALL, THE TREATY TOOK AWAY TERRITORY COMPRISING A QUARTER OF THE POPULATION AND INDUSTRY OF THE FORMER RUSSIAN EMPIRE.

cards.q: How does the first article of Brest differ from the preambles of the Paris treaties?
cards.a: Brest has no preamble and art. 1 states NEUTRALLY that the state of war has ended and the parties have resolved to live in peace. The Paris treaties, by contrast, explain in the very first paragraph of the preamble that THE STATE OF WAR AROSE FROM HOSTILITIES BEGUN BY THE CENTRAL POWER IN QUESTION — they apportion guilt at the outset.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What did Russia lose at Brest-Litovsk?
cards.a: Under art. 3 Poland, Lithuania, Courland and part of Livonia, with a 'limited right of self-determination under the supervision of Austria-Hungary and Germany'; in the Caucasus Ardahan, Kars and Batumi back to the Ottoman Empire; it had to demobilise, make peace with Ukraine and evacuate Estonia, Livonia, Finland and the Åland Islands. IN ALL, TERRITORY WITH A QUARTER OF THE POPULATION AND INDUSTRY of the former empire.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: The structure of the Paris treaties and where Sèvres differs
slides.text: All the main Paris treaties follow the structure of the TREATY OF VERSAILLES, which served as the TEMPLATE. THE FIRST PART (arts. 1–26) is in all of them the COVENANT OF THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS, because Wilson demanded that it be attached to Versailles. THE SECOND PART consists of provisions on the DELIMITATION OF THE NEW BORDERS (both Sèvres and St Germain set up BOUNDARY COMMISSIONS). THE THIRD PART is the POLITICAL CLAUSES — Versailles, St Germain and Trianon separate the provisions on Europe from those on extra-European interests (especially colonies); SÈVRES DOES NOT SEPARATE THEM. Several differences set Sèvres apart most: THE USA IS NOT A PARTY TO IT (it was never at war with the Ottoman Empire), so it does not speak of the 'Allied and ASSOCIATED' powers as the others do. And in the preamble: whereas the other treaties speak of a FIRM, JUST AND LASTING PEACE, IN THE FRENCH — THAT IS, THE AUTHORITATIVE — VERSION OF THE TREATY OF SÈVRES THE WORD 'JUST' IS MISSING. The very phrase PEACE TREATY is not mentioned in the original text of Sèvres. As to particulars: under ART. 36 Constantinople was to remain Turkish 'for the time being' and could therefore remain the seat of the sultan and the caliphate; under ARTS. 37–61 the STRAITS were placed under the international administration of a Straits Commission, the waters neutralised and the shores demilitarised; for KURDISTAN (arts. 62–64) the autonomous region was not settled in the treaty itself but left to a British-French-Italian commission; for SMYRNA a provisional autonomous status was envisaged, although Greece was to receive extensive administrative rights and could keep troops there, while the city was formally to remain part of Turkey.

cards.q: What is the common structure of the Paris peace treaties?
cards.a: The template was the TREATY OF VERSAILLES. The first part (arts. 1–26) is in all of them the COVENANT OF THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS (Wilson demanded its attachment); the second is the DELIMITATION OF BORDERS and boundary commissions; the third the POLITICAL CLAUSES; then military provisions, prisoners and graves, penalties, financial and economic provisions, aerial navigation, ports and railways — and the last part is the statute of the International Labour Organisation.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: Which word is missing from the preamble of the Treaty of Sèvres, and why is it worth noticing?
cards.a: The word 'JUST'. The other Paris treaties speak of a firm, JUST and lasting peace; in the French — that is, the authoritative — version of Sèvres it is missing. And the very phrase 'peace treaty' is not mentioned in the original text at all.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Nationality and 'ethnic disentanglement'
slides.text: Articles 123–131 of Sèvres on the nationality of the inhabitants of the former Ottoman Empire have no counterpart in Versailles or St Germain, BECAUSE THEY REST ON MIGRATION. Whereas St Germain built on Heimatrecht, here all former Ottoman citizens living in a new state on the territory of the former empire were AUTOMATICALLY TO ACQUIRE THE NATIONALITY OF THAT NEW STATE. ART. 125: any person WHOSE RACE DIFFERED FROM THE MAJORITY OF THE POPULATION of the territory concerned had the RIGHT TO OPT for Armenian, Azerbaijani, Georgian, Greek, Mesopotamian, Syrian, Bulgarian, Turkish or Hejazi nationality — PROVIDED THE MAJORITY OF THE POPULATION OF THE CHOSEN STATE BELONGED TO THE SAME RACE as the person opting. ART. 126 was then particularly important: WHOEVER OPTED HAD TO TRANSFER HIS RESIDENCE WITHIN TWELVE MONTHS TO THE STATE WHOSE NATIONALITY HE HAD CHOSEN — while being permitted to retain immovable property in the state from which he was in fact obliged to emigrate. ART. 129: JEWS LIVING WITHIN THE BOUNDARIES OF PALESTINE WERE IPSO FACTO TO BECOME PALESTINIAN CITIZENS and were thereby excluded from the other nationalities. Gassner sees something fundamental here: THOSE PROVISIONS FOCUS ON THE 'ETHNIC DISENTANGLEMENT' OF THE FORMER OTTOMAN POPULATION AND CAN THEREFORE BE REGARDED AS THE FIRST HARBINGERS OF THE POPULATION EXCHANGE ACTUALLY CARRIED OUT AFTER THE TREATY OF LAUSANNE IN 1923. And a second harbinger: ART. 143 obliged Greece and Turkey to conclude a special agreement on the RECIPROCAL AND VOLUNTARY EMIGRATION of the Turkish and Greek populations.

cards.q: How did Sèvres deal with nationality, and in what way does it foreshadow the later population exchange?
cards.a: Former Ottoman citizens automatically acquired the nationality of the new state in which they lived; anyone racially different from the majority could OPT for another nationality — but HAD TO TRANSFER HIS RESIDENCE WITHIN TWELVE MONTHS to the chosen state (art. 126). Those provisions aim at the 'ETHNIC DISENTANGLEMENT' of the population and are therefore the first harbinger of the POPULATION EXCHANGE carried out after the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923; art. 143 on the reciprocal emigration of Greeks and Turks points the same way.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Minority protection and article 88 on Austrian independence
slides.text: In St Germain, ARTS. 36–62 governed mainly boundary questions and relations with neighbours; for KLAGENFURT a PLEBISCITE was to be held on which state the territory would go to — IT IS INTERESTING THAT SÈVRES PROVIDES FOR NOTHING OF THE KIND. The 'HEART' of the political provisions of St Germain was ARTICLE 88 ON THE 'INALIENABLE INDEPENDENCE OF AUSTRIA' — THE ANSCHLUSSVERBOT. (The fourth part on Morocco, Egypt, Siam and China was simply copied from Versailles and, since Austria had no colonies, was without object.) MINORITY PROTECTION is incorporated in St Germain into the third part (arts. 62–82), whereas in Sèvres it forms a separate fourth part (arts. 140–151) — IN VERSAILLES THERE IS NO SUCH PART AT ALL. Both derive from the minority provisions of the 'LITTLE TREATY OF VERSAILLES' WITH POLAND of 28 June 1919, so they largely correspond; in Turkey's case it aimed chiefly at the GREEK, ARMENIAN AND JEWISH minorities. Minority protection in relation to the former Ottoman Empire was THREEFOLD: besides the provisions in Sèvres, a twenty-article minorities treaty was signed on 10 August 1920 between the principal powers and GREECE (for former Ottoman citizens in the parts allotted to Greece) and a corresponding treaty with ARMENIA. Particularly remarkable is ART. 144 OF SÈVRES: the so-called 'EMVAL-I-METROUKEH', the houses or businesses of Ottoman nationals OF NON-TURKISH RACE who had been FORCIBLY DRIVEN FROM THEIR HOMES OR HAD LEFT THEM IN FEAR OF MASSACRE, HAD TO BE RESTORED TO THE VICTIMS OF TURKISH AGGRESSION FREE OF CHARGE.

terms.def: Houses and businesses of Ottoman citizens of non-Turkish race who had been driven out or had fled in fear of massacre; art. 144 of Sèvres ordered their restitution free of charge.

cards.q: What did article 88 of the Treaty of St Germain govern?
cards.a: The 'INALIENABLE INDEPENDENCE OF AUSTRIA' — the Anschlussverbot, the prohibition of union with Germany. Gassner calls it the 'heart' of the treaty's political provisions.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What did minority protection in the Paris treaties derive from, and how was it arranged for Turkey?
cards.a: From the minority provisions of the 'LITTLE TREATY OF VERSAILLES' WITH POLAND of 28 June 1919. For the former Ottoman Empire it was THREEFOLD: the provisions in Sèvres, a separate minorities treaty with Greece (for Ottoman citizens in the parts allotted to Greece) and a corresponding treaty with Armenia. In Versailles there is no such part at all.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What did art. 144 of the Treaty of Sèvres order?
cards.a: That the so-called 'Emval-i-Metroukeh' — the houses and businesses of Ottoman citizens OF NON-TURKISH RACE who had been forcibly driven from their homes or had left them in fear of massacre — HAD TO BE RESTORED TO THE VICTIMS OF TURKISH AGGRESSION FREE OF CHARGE.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Military provisions, graves and war guilt
slides.text: The MILITARY PROVISIONS of Sèvres ordered the demobilisation of the Ottoman forces, the limitation of the military apparatus and an ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION OF AN AIR FORCE (art. 191). And the figures to compare: GROUND FORCES LIMITED TO 50,000 MEN IN SÈVRES, TO 100,000 IN VERSAILLES AND TO AT MOST 30,000 IN ST GERMAIN — given the territorial size of those three countries, THE TURKISH LIMITATIONS WERE THE HARSHEST. The PROVISIONS ON GRAVES differ markedly in Sèvres: ART. 218 required the Turkish government TO TRANSFER TO THE BRITISH, FRENCH AND ITALIAN GOVERNMENTS FULL AND EXCLUSIVE PROPERTY RIGHTS IN THE LAND WITHIN TURKEY WHERE THE GRAVES OF THEIR FALLEN LAY — in fact this affected only the GALLIPOLI PENINSULA, where more than 40,000 Allied soldiers died, chiefly from Australia and New Zealand. The SEVENTH PART, 'PENALTIES', is devoted to the punishment of war crimes and is almost identical with the other treaties — EXCEPT FOR ART. 230, WHICH CONCERNED THE GENOCIDE OF THE ARMENIAN MINORITY. And an innovation in the history of international law: the formulation of the so-called 'WAR GUILT ARTICLES' (ST GERMAIN ART. 177, VERSAILLES ART. 231, NEUILLY ART. 121), which established a FAR-REACHING, HITHERTO UNPRECEDENTED RESPONSIBILITY OF THE AGGRESSOR — in them the country concerned was made responsible as the author of the losses and damage suffered by the Allies. Sèvres does contain a war guilt article too (art. 231 para. 1), BUT THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE WAS ACCORDED ONLY A DIMINISHED RESPONSIBILITY, particularly because it had acted as a MERE AUXILIARY OF THE GERMAN EMPIRE. The reparation provisions have only an indirect counterpart in Sèvres: ART. 231 PARA. 2 FORMALLY RENOUNCED REPARATION CLAIMS — which stands in sharp contradiction to art. 235, which obliged the Turkish government to pay.

cards.q: Compare the limitations on ground forces in the three treaties.
cards.a: Sèvres 50,000 men, Versailles 100,000, St Germain at most 30,000 — and Sèvres additionally prohibited an air force absolutely (art. 191). Given the territorial size of the three countries, THE TURKISH LIMITATIONS WERE THE HARSHEST.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What is new about the 'war guilt articles', and how does Sèvres treat them?
cards.a: They were AN INNOVATION IN THE HISTORY OF INTERNATIONAL LAW: they established a far-reaching, hitherto unprecedented RESPONSIBILITY OF THE AGGRESSOR (St Germain art. 177, Versailles art. 231, Neuilly art. 121). Sèvres has such an article too, but it accords the OTTOMAN EMPIRE ONLY A DIMINISHED RESPONSIBILITY, since it acted as a mere auxiliary of Germany — and in art. 231 para. 2 it even formally renounces reparation claims.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What was special about art. 218 of the Treaty of Sèvres on graves?
cards.a: It required the Turkish government TO TRANSFER TO THE BRITISH, FRENCH AND ITALIAN GOVERNMENTS FULL AND EXCLUSIVE PROPERTY RIGHTS IN THE LAND where the graves of their fallen lay. In fact this affected only the Gallipoli peninsula, where more than 40,000 Allied soldiers died, chiefly from Australia and New Zealand.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

slides.title: Conclusion: what holds and what does not
slides.text: All three treaties stand IN THE SHADOW OF VERSAILLES, and yet they are essential components of the new world order. All mark THE END OF THE MULTI-ETHNIC EMPIRES, WHOSE POLITICAL SIGNIFICANCE HAD LAGGED FAR BEHIND THEIR TERRITORIAL EXTENT ALREADY BEFORE 1914. And the key formulation: THE COLLAPSE OF THE RUSSIAN, HABSBURG AND OTTOMAN EMPIRES HAD ALREADY TAKEN PLACE BEFORE THE TREATIES WERE EVEN SIGNED — PUT DIFFERENTLY, THE COLLAPSE OF ALL THREE EMPIRES WAS MERELY SEALED IN LAW BY THE RESPECTIVE PEACE TREATY. And the fate of the three texts: OF ALL THREE, ONLY THE TREATY OF ST GERMAIN ENTERED INTO FORCE — AND IT IS STILL IN FORCE TODAY, PARTLY AT CONSTITUTIONAL LEVEL. BREST-LITOVSK WAS ANNULLED BY THE GERMAN ARMISTICE IN NOVEMBER 1918, and SÈVRES, WHICH WAS NEVER RATIFIED, WAS ULTIMATELY REPLACED BY THE TREATY OF LAUSANNE IN 1923. Of all five main Paris treaties, SÈVRES DIFFERS THE MOST: at first sight its terms are not as harsh as those of Versailles, but ON SECOND LOOK IT IS CLEAR THAT HERE TOO THE ALLIES AIMED AT THE DEFEAT OF THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE — the symbol being THE OCCUPATION OF CONSTANTINOPLE, WHICH THE ALLIES OCCUPIED, UNLIKE VIENNA OR BERLIN. And a final sentence: in post-imperial Austria, Hungary and Turkey alike there arose EXTENSIVE PARAMILITARY SUBCULTURES shaped by the successive traumatising experience of WAR, DEFEAT AND TERRITORIAL DISINTEGRATION — and although the degree of violence in those territories differed considerably, THE LOGIC BEHIND THE VIOLENT CONDUCT DID NOT.

cards.q: Which of the three treaties entered into force and what became of the others?
cards.a: Only the TREATY OF ST GERMAIN — and it is still in force today, partly at constitutional level. BREST-LITOVSK was annulled by the German armistice in November 1918; SÈVRES was never ratified and was replaced in 1923 by the TREATY OF LAUSANNE.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What did the peace treaties actually do about the collapse of the three empires?
cards.a: They merely SEALED IT IN LAW. The collapse of the Russian, Habsburg and Ottoman empires had already taken place BEFORE THE TREATIES WERE SIGNED — and the political significance of those empires had lagged far behind their territorial extent already before 1914.
cards.topic: World War I and the Paris Peace Conference

cards.q: What connects post-imperial Austria, Hungary and Turkey?
cards.a: The emergence of EXTENSIVE PARAMILITARY SUBCULTURES shaped by the successive traumatising experience of WAR, DEFEAT AND TERRITORIAL DISINTEGRATION. And although the degree of violence in those territories differed considerably, THE LOGIC BEHIND THE VIOLENT CONDUCT DID NOT.
